It is important to maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription medications, as well as herbal products, and share this information with your doctor and pharmacist. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. In the United States, you can call 1-800-222-1222. Laboratory and Medical Tests: While using this medication, regular laboratory and medical tests, such as complete blood counts and liver function tests, should be conducted. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, consult your doctor or pharmacist promptly to establish a new dosing schedule. Storage: Store this medication in the refrigerator and do not freeze it. Keep it in its original container to protect it from light. Some brands of this medication may also be stored at room temperature if necessary. Consult your pharmacist or the product packaging to determine if your medication can be stored at room temperature and for how long. Discard any unused portion of the medication. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly dispose of this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Medical Alert: Your condition may cause complications in a medical emergency. Important Information: This document is a summary and does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Common Brand Names: This medication is available under various brand names, including Abrilada, Amjevita, Cyltezo, Hadlima, Hulio, Humira, Hyrimoz, Idacio, Simlandi, Yuflyma, and Yusimry. Warning: This medication can weaken your immune system, reducing your ability to fight infections. This effect may lead to serious, potentially fatal infections, such as fungal infections or bacterial infections, including tuberculosis. Inform your doctor of your medical history, particularly any past, recent, or current infections. Additionally, let your doctor know if you have lived or traveled in areas where certain fungal infections, such as coccidioidomycosis or histoplasmosis, are common, or if you have been in contact with someone with tuberculosis. These fungal infections are commonly found in regions such as the Ohio and Mississippi River valleys and the southwestern United States. Your doctor will test you for tuberculosis (TB) infection before and during treatment with this medication. Although rare, there is a risk, particularly in children, teens, and young adults, of developing cancers such as lymphoma or skin cancer due to this medication or your underlying medical condition. Discuss the risks and benefits of treatment with your doctor. Uses: Adalimumab is used to reduce pain and swelling associated with certain types of arthritis, including rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, juvenile idiopathic arthritis, and ankylosing spondylitis. It is also used to treat specific skin disorders, such as plaque-type psoriasis and hidradenitis suppurativa. This medication works by blocking a protein in the immune system called tumor necrosis factor (TNF), which contributes to joint swelling and damage in arthritis, as well as red, scaly patches in psoriasis. Adalimumab belongs to a class of drugs known as TNF blockers. How to Use: Read the Medication Guide and Instructions for Use provided by your pharmacist before starting adalimumab and each time you receive a refill. Consult your healthcare professional on how to prepare and use this medication. Inject this medication under the skin as directed by your doctor, typically every other week or, in some cases, once a week. The injection is administered in the thigh or abdomen. Dosage is based on your medical condition and response to treatment. For children, the dosage is also determined by weight. If you are using this medication to treat psoriasis, hidradenitis suppurativa, Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis, or uveitis, your doctor may prescribe a different schedule or higher dose at the start of treatment. Before injecting, remove the medication from the refrigerator 15 to 30 minutes in advance to allow it to reach room temperature. Do not warm the medication using other methods, such as a microwave or hot water. Inspect the product for particles or discoloration before use. If either is present, do not use the liquid. Clean the injection site with rubbing alcohol before each dose. Rotate the injection site each time to minimize skin injury, ensuring the new site is at least 5 centimeters away from the previous one. Avoid injecting into skin that is sore, bruised, red, or hard. To reduce bruising, do not rub the injection site after administration. Use this medication regularly to achieve the most benefit. To help you remember, mark the day on your calendar when you need to administer the medication. Redness, itching, pain, or swelling at the injection site may occur. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Liver Disease Risk: Adalimumab may rarely cause serious, potentially fatal liver disease in individuals exposed to the hepatitis B virus. Your doctor may order blood tests and monitor for symptoms during treatment and for several months after your last dose. Allergic Reactions: Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. However, this is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Precautions: Before using adalimumab, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, any adalimumab products, or any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients, such as natural rubber or latex, which can cause allergic reactions or other problems. Adalimumab can increase your susceptibility to infections or worsen existing infections. Avoid contact with individuals who have infections that can easily spread, such as chickenpox, COVID-19, measles, or the flu. Inform your healthcare professional that you are using adalimumab before receiving any immunizations or vaccinations. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary, as it may harm an unborn baby. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor. This medication passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist.
